lyra, lyrae f.

noun, first declension

The stringed instrument of Mercury and Apollo, smaller than the cithara.

Other words

  • testūdō, testūdinis f. — lyre (of tortoise shell)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 4.464; Hor. C. 3.11.3

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor.)

    The tortoise, and so the lyre whose sounding box was a tortoise shell.

  • fidēs, fidium f. pl. — a stringed instrument, lyre

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical

    The word of classical prose, always plural there: fidibus canere, play the lyre (Cic.).

Examples

  • asinus jacentem vīdit in prātō lyram. accessit et temptāvit chordās ungulā; sonuēre tāctae.

    a donkey saw a lyre lying in a meadow. He went up and tried the strings with his hoof; touched, they sounded.Phaedr. App. 14.1–3

See also harp, guitar, musical instrument, play.
